title.en: Granted, admittedly, be that as it may
title.es: Concedido, eso sí, sea como sea

es: Reconocer marcadores de concesión C1 (granted, admittedly, be that as it may, that said, even so) y localizar la réplica que sigue en un debate.

vocabulary.es: es cierto, lo admito (abre una concesión)

teaching.en: Granted, the plan has a drawback, since it would cost more in the short term, but it remains the most sensible option we have.
teaching.es: Es cierto que el plan tiene un inconveniente, ya que costaría más a corto plazo, pero sigue siendo la opción más sensata que tenemos.
teaching.explanationEs: Granted + coma reconoce un punto ajeno; la réplica llega después con but.
segments: Granted, the plan has a drawback, since it would cost more in
the short term, but it remains the most sensible option we have.
teaching.audioText: Granted, the plan has a drawback, since it would cost more in the short term, but it remains the most sensible option we have.

teaching.en: Admittedly, the price is high, but my opponent has failed to point out that the service is excellent and far better than anything else on offer.
teaching.es: Hay que admitir que el precio es alto, pero mi oponente no ha señalado que el servicio es excelente y mucho mejor que cualquier otra oferta.
teaching.explanationEs: Admittedly admite una debilidad y va al principio; point out saca a la luz un dato que el otro omitió.
segments: Admittedly, the price is high, but my opponent has failed to point out
that the service is excellent and far better than anything else on offer.
teaching.audioText: Admittedly, the price is high, but my opponent has failed to point out that the service is excellent and far better than anything else on offer.

teaching.en: Be that as it may, my opponent has still not answered the question about who will pay for the changes.
teaching.es: Sea como sea, mi oponente sigue sin responder a la pregunta sobre quién pagará los cambios.
teaching.explanationEs: Be that as it may abre la réplica sin but: ya marca el contraste por sí solo.
segments: Be that as it may, my opponent has still not
answered the question about who will pay for the changes.
teaching.audioText: Be that as it may, my opponent has still not answered the question about who will pay for the changes.

teaching.en: That said, the drawback is small compared with the benefits, and all the same it deserves an honest answer.
teaching.es: Dicho esto, el inconveniente es pequeño comparado con los beneficios, y aun así merece una respuesta honesta.
teaching.explanationEs: That said matiza lo que acabas de conceder; all the same subraya que, pese a todo, tu postura sigue en pie.
segments: That said, the drawback is small compared with the benefits,
and all the same it deserves an honest answer.
teaching.audioText: That said, the drawback is small compared with the benefits, and all the same it deserves an honest answer.

teaching.en: The team lost the first point; even so, it went on to win the debate, because the judges valued its calm, well-evidenced replies.
teaching.es: El equipo perdió el primer punto; aun así, terminó ganando el debate, porque los jueces valoraron sus réplicas serenas y bien fundamentadas.
teaching.explanationEs: Even so va en la réplica, después de un punto que ya se ha concedido.
segments: The team lost the first point; even so, it went on to
win the debate, because the judges valued its calm, well-evidenced replies.
teaching.audioText: The team lost the first point; even so, it went on to win the debate, because the judges valued its calm, well-evidenced replies.

teaching.en: To be fair, my opponent is right about the cost, and I am happy to concede that point before turning to the benefits.
teaching.es: Para ser justos, mi oponente tiene razón sobre el coste, y concedo ese punto con gusto antes de pasar a los beneficios.
teaching.explanationEs: To be fair introduce un reconocimiento leal; concede es el verbo formal para admitir un punto.
segments: To be fair, my opponent is right about the cost, and I
am happy to concede that point before turning to the benefits.
teaching.audioText: To be fair, my opponent is right about the cost, and I am happy to concede that point before turning to the benefits.

prompt.es: Lee la intervención. ¿Qué concede el orador y cómo recupera su postura?

choices.text: He denies the longer day, then argues that pupils are rested.
He admits that pupils are tired, then argues that the day is shorter.
He admits the longer day, then argues that rest matters more.

feedback.es: Granted reconoce que el día terminaría más tarde; That said devuelve la discusión a su tesis: dormir más pesa más.

hint.es: Busca qué sigue a Granted y qué aporta That said.

origin.text: Granted, the new timetable would end the day later. That said, pupils would arrive more rested, and that matters more than an hour of free time.

prompt.es: Completa: «Aun así, el plan sigue teniendo un grave inconveniente.»

feedback.es: Even so es la fórmula fija para una réplica tras un punto ya concedido.

hint.es: Sigue a la concesión y va con so: aun así.

origin.text: The figures look good, and I do not deny it. ___ so, the plan still has a serious drawback.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Es cierto que el precio es alto, pero la calidad es excelente.»

answer.text: Granted, the price is high, but the quality is excellent

feedback.es: Granted abre la concesión con coma y but introduce la réplica.

hint.es: Empieza por la palabra que concede un punto.

prompt.es: Escucha el resumen y elige qué concede el oponente.

choices.text: That pollution is a serious problem.
That the health costs of doing nothing are far higher.
That the council could pay the shops back.

feedback.es: El oponente dice «granted, pollution is a serious problem»: esa es su concesión; después replica con el problema de las tiendas.

origin.audio: In last night's debate on closing the city centre to cars, the first speaker argued that cleaner air would save lives. Her opponent replied that, granted, pollution is a serious problem; that said, small shops would lose customers, and he doubted that the council could pay them back. Admittedly, the first speaker said, some shops would lose money. Be that as it may, she added, the health costs of doing nothing are far higher.

prompt.es: Escucha otra vez y elige cómo responde la primera oradora a lo de las tiendas.

choices.text: She admits the risk and agrees to postpone the plan until shops are ready.
She admits the risk but argues that doing nothing costs more in health.
She answers that the losses of the shops are smaller than he claims.

feedback.es: Admittedly reconoce el riesgo para las tiendas y Be that as it may la devuelve a su tesis: no actuar cuesta más en salud.

origin.audio: In last night's debate on closing the city centre to cars, the first speaker argued that cleaner air would save lives. Her opponent replied that, granted, pollution is a serious problem; that said, small shops would lose customers, and he doubted that the council could pay them back. Admittedly, the first speaker said, some shops would lose money. Be that as it may, she added, the health costs of doing nothing are far higher.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada expresión con su función en un debate.

pairs.es: Concedes una debilidad y la réplica sigue con but

pairs: Be that as it may, the fee stays.

pairs.es: Replicas sin but, cerrando el punto concedido

pairs: To be fair, my opponent is right.

pairs.es: Reconoces con lealtad el acierto del contrario

pairs: I would point out that costs fell.

pairs.es: Señalas un dato que el otro ha omitido

feedback.es: Cada fórmula cumple un papel distinto: conceder con but, replicar sin but, reconocer con lealtad y señalar un dato omitido.

prompt.es: Escucha la intervención y elige qué reconoce la oradora sobre el coste.

choices.text: That the plan will stay more expensive for years to come.
That the plan will cost more than her opponent has claimed.
That the plan will be more expensive at the start.

feedback.es: «Granted, it will cost the council more in the first year» es la concesión: el sobrecoste se limita al primer año, no a toda la vida del plan.

origin.audio: The proposal is not perfect. Granted, it will cost the council more in the first year. That said, every serious study points the same way, and my opponent has offered nothing but anecdotes. Even so, I am willing to concede that the timetable needs another look.

prompt.es: Escucha otra vez y elige qué postura mantiene hacia su oponente.

choices.text: She finds his case weak, yet stays open to adjustments.
She finds his case weak and sees no reason to reconsider anything.
She thinks his case is strong but refuses to admit it in public.

feedback.es: Dice que solo ofrece anécdotas (caso débil), pero concede que el horario merece otra revisión: firme, aunque abierta.

origin.audio: The proposal is not perfect. Granted, it will cost the council more in the first year. That said, every serious study points the same way, and my opponent has offered nothing but anecdotes. Even so, I am willing to concede that the timetable needs another look.

prompt.es: Completa: «Para ser justos, el otro bando ha puesto a prueba la idea con más cuidado.»

feedback.es: To be fair es la fórmula fija para reconocer con lealtad el mérito del contrario antes de replicar.

origin.text: ___ be fair, the other side has tested the idea far more carefully than we have, and nobody here should pretend otherwise.

prompt.es: Lee el intercambio. ¿Qué hace Sara con su respuesta?

choices.text: She dismisses Tom's concern but admits that the buses would be popular.
She accepts Tom's concern but questions whether the solution is affordable.
She shares Tom's view and asks the council to accept his proposal.

feedback.es: Granted reconoce que el tráfico es un problema y Be that as it may desplaza la discusión al coste de la solución.

origin.text: Tom argues that free buses would cut traffic. Sara replies: 'Granted, traffic is a problem. Be that as it may, free buses would cost millions, and the council has no plan to pay for them.'

prompt.es: Lee el texto. ¿Qué deja entrever Tom con «all the same»?

choices.text: That the improvement in the air is too small to matter to him.
That people from the outer areas would gladly take the bus.
That the benefit does not remove his objection to the plan.

feedback.es: All the same indica que, aun aceptando la mejora del aire, su objeción sigue en pie.

origin.text: Mia says the city should ban cars. Tom answers that, admittedly, the air would improve; all the same, he doubts that people from the outer areas could reach the centre by bus.

prompt.es: Completa: «Estaba dispuesto a conceder que el plan tenía un inconveniente.»

feedback.es: Concede es el verbo formal para admitir un punto sin abandonar la postura.

origin.text: He was willing to ___ that the plan had a drawback, but he refused to admit that it was a mistake.

prompt.es: Escucha la intervención y elige con qué propósito menciona la omisión.

choices.text: To argue that her case is not complete despite its fair point.
To praise her for being careful about the cost of the plan.
To prove that older residents dislike her plan.

feedback.es: Tras conceder el punto sobre el coste, señala lo que ella omitió para sugerir que su argumento no está completo.

origin.audio: Carlos began by thanking everyone for coming. Admittedly, he said, the first speaker had made a fair point about cost, and he would not deny it. That said, he noted that she had not mentioned the benefits for older residents, and that gap, he suggested, made her whole argument weaker.

es: Usar hence, thereby, in so doing y whereby para expresar consecuencia y medio en registro formal.

vocabulary.es: por el cual, mediante el cual

teaching.en: The council introduced a fee for private cars; hence the sharp drop in traffic, which surprised even its most committed critics.
teaching.es: El ayuntamiento introdujo una tarifa para los autos particulares; de ahí el fuerte descenso del tráfico, que sorprendió incluso a sus críticos más convencidos.
teaching.explanationEs: Hence + nombre (o una oración) da la consecuencia; es formal y se usa al escribir.
segments: The council introduced a fee for private cars; hence the sharp
drop in traffic, which surprised even its most committed critics.
teaching.audioText: The council introduced a fee for private cars; hence the sharp drop in traffic, which surprised even its most committed critics.

teaching.en: The council charges a fee to discourage drivers, thereby reducing traffic and, in turn, improving the air that residents breathe.
teaching.es: El ayuntamiento cobra una tarifa para desalentar a los conductores, con lo cual reduce el tráfico y, a su vez, mejora el aire que respiran los residentes.
teaching.explanationEs: Thereby + verbo en -ing expresa el resultado de la acción anterior; in turn enlaza un resultado con el siguiente.
segments: The council charges a fee to discourage drivers, thereby reducing
traffic and, in turn, improving the air that residents breathe.
teaching.audioText: The council charges a fee to discourage drivers, thereby reducing traffic and, in turn, improving the air that residents breathe.

teaching.en: The council created a scheme whereby residents pay only half the fee, provided that they can prove they live inside the zone.
teaching.es: El ayuntamiento creó un plan por el cual los residentes pagan solo la mitad de la tarifa, siempre que puedan demostrar que viven dentro de la zona.
teaching.explanationEs: Whereby (= by which) presenta el sistema o la regla con la que algo funciona.
segments: The council created a scheme whereby residents pay only half the
fee, provided that they can prove they live inside the zone.
teaching.audioText: The council created a scheme whereby residents pay only half the fee, provided that they can prove they live inside the zone.

teaching.en: The council lowered the fee for residents. In so doing, it won their support and helped to curb the opposition that had formed.
teaching.es: El ayuntamiento bajó la tarifa para los residentes. Al hacerlo, ganó su apoyo y ayudó a frenar la oposición que se había formado.
teaching.explanationEs: In so doing retoma la acción anterior y da su resultado; el sujeto es el mismo. Curb = frenar.
segments: The council lowered the fee for residents. In so doing, it won
their support and helped to curb the opposition that had formed.
teaching.audioText: The council lowered the fee for residents. In so doing, it won their support and helped to curb the opposition that had formed.

teaching.en: The levy is cheap to run and easy to explain, hence its popularity among officials who need results before the next election.
teaching.es: La tasa es barata de gestionar y fácil de explicar; de ahí su popularidad entre los funcionarios que necesitan resultados antes de las próximas elecciones.
teaching.explanationEs: Hence puede ir delante de un nombre sin verbo: hence its popularity. Levy es una tasa impuesta por una autoridad.
segments: The levy is cheap to run and easy to explain, hence
its popularity among officials who need results before the next election.
teaching.audioText: The levy is cheap to run and easy to explain, hence its popularity among officials who need results before the next election.

teaching.en: The fee pays for new buses, thereby helping commuters, and it gives drivers a genuine incentive to leave their cars at home.
teaching.es: La tarifa paga autobuses nuevos, con lo cual ayuda a quienes viajan a diario, y da a los conductores un incentivo real para dejar el auto en casa.
teaching.explanationEs: Thereby helping: la ayuda es la consecuencia directa de pagar los autobuses; incentive es lo que motiva un cambio.
segments: The fee pays for new buses, thereby helping commuters, and it
gives drivers a genuine incentive to leave their cars at home.
teaching.audioText: The fee pays for new buses, thereby helping commuters, and it gives drivers a genuine incentive to leave their cars at home.

prompt.es: Elige la frase que une acción y resultado con el conector formal correcto.

choices.text: The city raised parking charges, thereby discouraging short car trips.
The city raised parking charges, thereby it discouraged short car trips.
The city raised parking charges, hence discouraging short car trips.

feedback.es: Thereby va seguido de un verbo en -ing; con una oración completa o con hence el conector no funciona.

hint.es: Thereby pide un verbo en -ing; hence pide un nombre o una oración.

origin.text: The city wanted fewer short car journeys in the centre, so it raised the price of parking in every street.

prompt.es: Completa: «…de ahí su popularidad entre los funcionarios.»

feedback.es: Hence + nombre expresa una consecuencia en registro formal: hence its popularity.

hint.es: Conector formal para «de ahí», seguido directamente de un nombre.

origin.text: The levy costs little to collect, and the scheme is easy to explain, ___ its popularity with officials.

prompt.es: Ordena: «El ayuntamiento bajó la tarifa y, al hacerlo, ganó apoyo.»

answer.text: The council lowered the fee and, in so doing, won support

feedback.es: In so doing retoma la acción de bajar la tarifa y presenta su resultado: ganó apoyo.

hint.es: In so doing va entre comas, después de la acción que retoma.

prompt.es: Escucha la noticia y elige quién paga menos por entrar en el centro.

choices.text: The visitors, who will pay only after two years.
The residents, who will pay half of the daily fee.
The drivers of buses, who do not pay the levy.

feedback.es: Los residentes pagarán la mitad de la tarifa diaria; los visitantes pagan las cinco libras completas.

origin.audio: The council has announced a scheme whereby drivers entering the centre will pay a daily fee of five pounds. Officials say the levy will discourage short car journeys, thereby curbing traffic and, in turn, improving the air. Residents will pay half, which the council hopes will reduce opposition. The money will pay for new bus routes within two years, hence the confident mood of the transport department.

prompt.es: Escucha otra vez y elige por qué el ayuntamiento rebaja la tarifa a los residentes.

choices.text: To improve the air in the quiet streets of the centre.
To pay for the new bus routes much more quickly.
To win over local people who might reject the scheme.

feedback.es: El ayuntamiento espera que la rebaja reduzca la oposición: su propósito es suavizar la resistencia de los vecinos.

prompt.es: Escucha la noticia y elige qué sostienen los críticos sobre la caída del tráfico.

choices.text: That higher petrol prices, not cheaper bus fares, are the main cause.
That cheaper fares came too late to affect traffic this year.
That the council has exaggerated the fall in traffic this year.

feedback.es: Los críticos atribuyen la caída al precio de la gasolina, no a la rebaja de las tarifas del autobús.

origin.audio: The council has cut bus fares by a third, thereby encouraging more people to leave their cars at home. Hence the fall in traffic this year, although critics argue that the main reason is the price of petrol. In so doing, the council has also lowered its own income, and nobody can yet say how it will balance the budget.

prompt.es: Escucha otra vez y elige qué inquietud deja ver la última frase.

choices.text: That the council will raise fares again next year.
That cheaper fares may create a funding problem.
That fewer drivers will mean fewer bus passengers.

feedback.es: Al bajar las tarifas del autobús el ayuntamiento ingresa menos y nadie sabe cómo equilibrará el presupuesto: hay un posible problema de financiación.

origin.audio: The council has cut bus fares by a third, thereby encouraging more people to leave their cars at home. Hence the fall in traffic this year, although critics argue that the main reason is the price of petrol. In so doing, the council has also lowered its own income, and nobody can yet say how it will balance the budget.

prompt.es: Completa: «El club tiene un plan por el cual los socios nuevos no pagan el primer mes.»

feedback.es: Whereby (= by which) presenta la regla o el sistema con el que funciona un programa.

origin.text: The club has a scheme ___ new members pay nothing during their first month.

prompt.es: Lee el informe. ¿Con qué propósito repite el autor «hence»?

choices.text: To argue that the concern of the shops outweighs the scheme's success.
To prove that shops and residents have the same interests.
To present two different results as consequences of the same success.

feedback.es: Las dos frases empiezan con hence: la ampliación del plan y la inquietud de las tiendas son consecuencias del mismo éxito.

origin.text: The scheme has been a success, hence the decision to use it in other streets too. Hence, too, the concern of the shops, which fear that fewer cars will mean fewer customers.

prompt.es: Lee el texto. ¿Qué sugiere el último comentario de los críticos?

choices.text: That charging only visitors is unfair and may drive tourists away.
That free entry will soon make the centre too crowded for everyone.
That visitors will soon be charged much less than local residents.

feedback.es: Los críticos sostienen que la entrada gratuita de los residentes traslada el coste a los visitantes, y vinculan eso con la caída de turistas: lo ven injusto y contraproducente.

origin.text: Residents whose homes lie inside the zone pay nothing, whereas visitors pay the full fee. The council argues that this is a scheme whereby local people are protected, thereby keeping the centre alive. Critics reply that free entry for residents merely shifts the cost on to visitors, hence the falling number of tourists.

prompt.es: Completa: «La tarifa busca desalentar a los conductores, no recaudar dinero.»

feedback.es: Discourage significa desalentar: la tarifa busca que los conductores no entren, no recaudar.

origin.text: The fee is meant to ___ drivers from entering the centre, not to raise money for the council.

prompt.es: Escucha el discurso y elige qué actitud muestra la alcaldesa ante las críticas.

choices.text: She listens politely to the critics but privately doubts the scheme.
She stands firm and does not plan to change course.
She is open to negotiating with the critics before making a decision.

feedback.es: «Whatever the critics may say» muestra que mantiene el plan sin cambiar de rumbo.

origin.audio: The mayor defended the levy. She said it was never meant to hurt drivers, but to give them a reason to think twice. In so doing, she argued, the city would reach its air targets years ahead of schedule, hence her firm wish that the scheme should stay, whatever the critics may say.

title.es: Seguir un debate a dos voces

es: Seguir un debate breve y construir un mapa con argumento, contraargumento, concesión y cierre.

teaching.en: The moderator reads the motion aloud and gives each speaker two minutes, then reminds the audience to weigh up the arguments before voting.
teaching.es: La moderadora lee la moción en voz alta y da dos minutos a cada orador; luego recuerda al público que sopese los argumentos antes de votar.
teaching.explanationEs: El moderador dirige el debate; la moción es la frase que se discute; weigh up = sopesar.
segments: The moderator reads the motion aloud and gives each speaker two minutes,
then reminds the audience to weigh up the arguments before voting.
teaching.audioText: The moderator reads the motion aloud and gives each speaker two minutes, then reminds the audience to weigh up the arguments before voting.

teaching.en: The motion is that mobile phones should be banned in class, and Tom is in favour of it, although his stance is more nuanced than it sounds.
teaching.es: La moción es que se prohíban los teléfonos celulares en clase, y Tom está a favor, aunque su postura es más matizada de lo que parece.
teaching.explanationEs: In favour of = a favor de; stance es la postura que alguien defiende.
segments: The motion is that mobile phones should be banned in class, and Tom is
in favour of it, although his stance is more nuanced than it sounds.
teaching.audioText: The motion is that mobile phones should be banned in class, and Tom is in favour of it, although his stance is more nuanced than it sounds.

teaching.en: Ana is against the motion, and her main contention is that phones are useful tools, provided that teachers set clear limits.
teaching.es: Ana está en contra de la moción y su tesis principal es que los teléfonos son herramientas útiles, siempre que los profesores pongan límites claros.
teaching.explanationEs: Against va sin preposición detrás: against the motion; contention es la tesis que alguien defiende con sus razones.
segments: Ana is against the motion, and her main contention is that
phones are useful tools, provided that teachers set clear limits.
teaching.audioText: Ana is against the motion, and her main contention is that phones are useful tools, provided that teachers set clear limits.

teaching.en: Tom's counterargument is that the premise behind Ana's case, that students use phones only for study, is simply unrealistic.
teaching.es: El contraargumento de Tom es que la premisa del caso de Ana, que los estudiantes usan el teléfono solo para estudiar, es sencillamente poco realista.
teaching.explanationEs: El contraargumento responde a lo que dijo el otro orador; la premisa es la idea que se da por supuesta.
segments: Tom's counterargument is that the premise behind Ana's case, that
students use phones only for study, is simply unrealistic.
teaching.audioText: Tom's counterargument is that the premise behind Ana's case, that students use phones only for study, is simply unrealistic.

teaching.en: Both speakers eventually find some common ground, yet each expects the other to carry the burden of proof, and their closing statements still differ on whether a total ban is necessary.
teaching.es: Ambos oradores acaban encontrando cierto terreno común, pero cada uno espera que el otro cargue con la carga de la prueba, y sus declaraciones de cierre siguen difiriendo sobre si hace falta una prohibición total.
teaching.explanationEs: Common ground = lo que ambos aceptan; burden of proof = quién debe demostrar su tesis; closing statement: la frase final donde cada orador resume su postura.
segments: Both speakers eventually find some common ground, yet each expects the other to carry the burden
of proof, and their closing statements still differ on whether a total ban is necessary.
teaching.audioText: Both speakers eventually find some common ground, yet each expects the other to carry the burden of proof, and their closing statements still differ on whether a total ban is necessary.

teaching.en: To sum up, the debate shows that the motion divides the class, and a good moderator records each argument fairly.
teaching.es: En resumen, el debate demuestra que la moción divide a la clase, y un buen moderador recoge cada argumento con justicia.
teaching.explanationEs: To sum up abre el resumen final; es la señal del cierre.
segments: To sum up, the debate shows that the motion divides
the class, and a good moderator records each argument fairly.
teaching.audioText: To sum up, the debate shows that the motion divides the class, and a good moderator records each argument fairly.

prompt.es: Lee la intervención. ¿Qué papel cumple dentro del mapa del debate?

choices.text: It answers what the previous speaker claimed.
It states her position and gives one reason for it.
It summarises both sides at the end of the debate.

feedback.es: Ana toma postura (against the motion) y da una razón: es un argumento, no una respuesta ni un cierre.

hint.es: Comprueba si la frase toma postura y aporta una razón.

origin.text: Ana is against the motion. Her argument is that phones help students look up information quickly and organise their homework.

answer.text: Dear editor, thank you for your letter. I take your point about sleep, and I would not deny that many teenagers arrive at school tired. Nonetheless, the evidence you quote comes from a single school, so the claim does not hold up. With respect, a later start would also end the day after five, which would leave little time for sport, homework or part-time work. While the idea has some merit, it would be hard for parents who start work early and for the buses that bring pupils to school. To rebut your main argument, look at the schools that already use a new timetable: most pupils adapt within a few weeks, and their results barely change. On the contrary, it would be unfair to overstate the problem. I therefore hope that the council will think again before it changes anything. Yours faithfully, Ana
accepted: Dear editor, thank you for your letter. I take your point about sleep, and I would not deny that many teenagers arrive at school tired. Nonetheless, the evidence you quote comes from a single school, so the claim does not hold up. With respect, a later start would also end the day after five, which would leave little time for sport, homework or part-time work. While the idea has some merit, it would be hard for parents who start work early and for the buses that bring pupils to school. To rebut your main argument, look at the schools that already use a new timetable: most pupils adapt within a few weeks, and their results barely change. On the contrary, it would be unfair to overstate the problem. I therefore hope that the council will think again before it changes anything. Yours faithfully, Ana

Dear editor, I take your point about tiredness, and I would not deny that sleep matters for pupils. Nonetheless, the evidence in your letter comes from only one school, and with respect, that does not prove very much. While a later start could help some teenagers, it would also end the day after five, so pupils would lose time for sport, for homework and for work. There is some merit in your idea, but the claim does not hold up when we look at schools that already use a new timetable, where most pupils adapt quickly. To rebut your main argument, I would ask for more evidence before we change the whole school day. On the contrary, it would be a mistake to overstate the problem. I hope that the council will think carefully before it decides. Yours faithfully, Carlos

prompt.es: Escucha la intervención y elige qué postura defiende la oradora.

choices.text: That the centre should be free of cars at weekends.
That traders should decide the opening hours of the centre.
That the centre should be free of cars every day.

feedback.es: Su postura es que el centro no tenga autos los fines de semana (car-free at weekends).

origin.audio: I would like to begin by thanking the chair. My position is simple: our centre should be car-free at weekends. Admittedly, some traders fear losing customers. Even so, cities that have tried it report more visitors, not fewer, and shops that adapted their opening hours did better than before.

prompt.es: Escucha otra vez: ¿qué deja entrever sobre las tiendas que adaptaron sus horarios?

choices.text: That opening hours matter more than the cars themselves.
That the fear of losing customers is often overstated.
That traders were right to fear losing their customers.

feedback.es: Si las tiendas que adaptaron sus horarios mejoraron, el miedo a perder clientes suele estar exagerado.

prompt.es: Completa: «…pero, en conjunto, hacen el centro más seguro.»

feedback.es: On balance es la fórmula fija para sopesar ambos lados y llegar a una conclusión.

origin.text: Pedestrian streets may cost some shops customers; ___ balance, however, they make the centre safer for everyone.

prompt.es: Escribe tu turno en el panel: apertura, concesión, refutación y cierre.

answer.text: Thank you, chair. My position is clear: the city centre should be closed to cars at weekends. Granted, congestion is a real problem, and some shops fear that they will lose customers. Nonetheless, the evidence from other cities suggests that pedestrian streets bring more visitors, thereby helping shops rather than harming them. Hence the growing support among parents, who want safer streets for their children. With respect, my opponent says that free buses would be a better solution, but that plan would cost too much and may not prove viable. Admittedly, a car-free centre involves a trade-off, yet on balance the benefits outweigh the costs. A scheme whereby residents keep access to their homes would protect the people who live here. In so doing, the council would show that it listens to both sides. To sum up, we should tackle traffic now, before urban life becomes impossible. Thank you.
accepted: Thank you, chair. My position is clear: the city centre should be closed to cars at weekends. Granted, congestion is a real problem, and some shops fear that they will lose customers. Nonetheless, the evidence from other cities suggests that pedestrian streets bring more visitors, thereby helping shops rather than harming them. Hence the growing support among parents, who want safer streets for their children. With respect, my opponent says that free buses would be a better solution, but that plan would cost too much and may not prove viable. Admittedly, a car-free centre involves a trade-off, yet on balance the benefits outweigh the costs. A scheme whereby residents keep access to their homes would protect the people who live here. In so doing, the council would show that it listens to both sides. To sum up, we should tackle traffic now, before urban life becomes impossible. Thank you.

Thank you, chair. I am against a full ban on cars in the centre, and I would like to explain why. To be fair, my opponent is right that congestion is a problem, and I would not deny that pedestrian streets are safer. That said, the evidence from our own city shows that shops lost much of their takings when a nearby street closed. Hence the concern of traders, who cannot wait for years to see whether visitors return. Even so, I am willing to concede that some streets could close, thereby giving families more space. A scheme whereby residents and traders vote street by street would be more viable than a single decision for the whole centre. With respect, a trade-off that ignores the people who work here is not a fair one. On balance, I believe that we should test one street first and tackle congestion step by step. Thank you.

feedback.es: Un buen turno encadena postura, concesión, refutación con evidencia y conector formal, y cierra sopesando ambos lados.

origin.text: Participas en un panel sobre movilidad urbana. Escribe en inglés (entre 170 y 250 palabras) tu turno: una apertura con tu postura, una concesión, una refutación con evidencia y un conector formal (hence, thereby, whereby, in so doing) y un cierre con on balance o to sum up.

prompt.es: Lee el extracto. ¿Qué hace el orador con la última frase?

choices.text: He concedes that the change is easy but doubts that it is worth it.
He admits the costs and proposes to delay the change for several years.
He admits that the change has costs yet defends it overall.

feedback.es: «That is not to say the change is easy» concede los costes y «on balance» mantiene su defensa del cambio.

origin.text: My opponent claims that pedestrian streets would empty the centre. The evidence shows the opposite: where they were introduced, the number of visitors rose. That is not to say the change is easy, but on balance the cost is worth paying.

prompt.es: Completa: «Los beneficios en seguridad superan claramente esa pequeña molestia.»

feedback.es: Outweigh significa pesar más que: lo que se gana supera lo que se sacrifica.

origin.text: Some visitors will lose a few minutes each day, but the gains in safety clearly ___ that small inconvenience.

prompt.es: Escucha el cierre y elige qué sugiere la presidenta sobre el debate.

choices.text: That the debate was about solutions, and that she favours a trial.
That the speakers agreed on the cost but disagreed about the problem.
That she wants more slogans so that the public pays attention.

feedback.es: Nadie negó la congestión: el desacuerdo era sobre las soluciones y ella prefiere un plan de prueba a más eslóganes.

origin.audio: The chair closed the panel by thanking the speakers. She noted that nobody had denied the problem of congestion; the disagreement was about how to tackle it, and at what price. In her view, the public would be better served by a trial scheme than by more slogans.
